name: 1605–1613 Indiana Avenue — the Thompson-Reid and Collins Bros. ice-cream works, building (district draft; refined by T-1946)

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '4-storey brick factory from Indiana Avenue to the alley, lettered THOMPSON-REID & COLLINS BROS. ICE CREAM CO., 'STABLE 2nd', an engine and a generator at its alley end'. On the target date the works are being built (T-3130). Collins Bros. and the Thompson-Reid company bought 1605-1613 in September 1903 for a plant covering the whole ground (chicago_tribune_1903_09_04_ice_cream_plant). In November 1903 the Tribune describes it as a four-storey brick building with a barn, 100 by 177 feet, from A. R. Buckley's plans (chicago_tribune_1903_11_08_ice_cream_works_begun). Its foundation was still being dug on 22 March 1904 (abendpost_1904_03_22_indiana_1605_foundation). From 1 September 1904 Thompson-Reid let a floor of its old Wabash Avenue premises (chicago_tribune_1904_09_11_thompson_reid_lease). So on 1 July 1904 the works were a building rising on the 1911 footprint, not yet the factory the sheet letters. The function is the plant the walls were for; 'large_workshop' is the closed vocabulary's nearest term for a manufactory. Carried to 1904 on the T-3019 census ruling (phase_unresolved). How high the walls stood is RECONSTRUCTED (liberty L-draft-indiana-1605-works-3130): three of the four storeys, and part of the fourth along the street. No dated source gives the walls' height. The dates either side frame it: a foundation was being dug on 22 March 1904, and the firm let a floor of its old premises from 1 September 1904. Three storeys is the draft's reading of a brick shell about fourteen weeks after its excavation, with the move about two months off.

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3130, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1946 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 20w trace (s20wfp-indiana_1605-b1), the T-3019 census (s20w-1605-front) and the T-1837 register row frontage-20w-1605–1613 (Brick factory); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-indiana-1605-works-3130).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-3019 census rules it present in 1904 (phase_unresolved). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row '(default)' overlaid with the frontage row: The Thompson-Reid and Collins Bros. ice-cream works RISING on 1 July 1904 (T-3130), in the working phase the census leaves open (phase_unresolved) and the draft declares, as 2126's Robbins house is declared. It stands on the 1911 sheet's outline of the finished factory, which agrees with the Tribune's 100 by 177 feet. The brick shell is three storeys up over its stone foundation, the street wall and its front returns 1.6 m into the fourth. The openings are empty, and there is no roof. A deck is laid at the first floor, with a pole scaffold along the street. The eight bays and the central opening are the draft's: no picture of the building is known. The 1886 houses are not stood, and the finished 1911 factory is not carried back. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 3679707877 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
